title: Protocol for observing microtubules and microtubule ends in both fixed and live primary microglia cells
protocol: Use ImageJ for level adjustments of frame brightness and contrast, and background subtraction for image preparation.
Open the movie obtained by recording SiR-tubulin labeled microglia using ImageJ.
Invert LUT using ImageJ dedicated command.
Select a “substack” to extract from a stack a selected image in which microtubules are clearly visible.
From “Image” menu, select “Stacks”, then “Tools” and “Make substack”.
Select one microtubule that is visible for the duration of the entire substack.
Choose a reference point that is stable for the duration of the entire substack and make a note of its XY coordinates.
Starting from the reference point, trace a line using the “Freehand line” tool, outlining the microtubule entire length.
Draw the microtubule for future reference.
Measure the length of the selection with the "Measure" command.
Change frame and repeat measurements until the end of the "substack".
Copy the values into an Excel file.
Starting from the second frame, measure the difference in length with the previous frame.
Note if the difference represents a “growth” (positive value), “shrinkage” (negative value) or “pausing” (value ≤ 0.5 μm).
For each “growth” or “shrinkage” event, divide the absolute value by the time interval between frames to obtain a rate in μm/s.
Average all growth and shrinkage rates to obtain an average rate in μm/s.
Count the number of “growth”, “shrinkage” or “pausing” events.
Divide each count by the total number of events to obtain percentages for “growth”, “shrinkage” and “pausing”.
Calculate the total time of analysis (in seconds) by multiplying the number of frames by the time interval between frames.
Count the number of transitions between “growth” and “shrinkage” (catastrophe) and vice versa (rescue).
Calculate catastrophe or rescue frequency by dividing the number of events by the product of the percentage and total time.
Calculate microtubule dynamicity by dividing the sum of event absolute numbers by the total time.
Draw a line carefully, comparing successive frames through the entire video to follow the behavior of the entire microtube.
Use ImageJ to open the movie obtained by recording EB3-EGFP comets in expressing microglia.
Invert LUT using ImageJ dedicated command.
Select a substack based on planes where the signal is bright and EB3 comets are clearly trackable.
With the “Segmented line” tool, select the section to be analyzed by the Kymograph plugin.
Adjust the line width to cover the region that will be analyzed.
From the ImageJ Plugin menu, select “Kymograph” and then “Kymograph builder”.
Check the original file properties from the “Image” menu to ensure pixel-micron conversion values are correct.
Calculate the percentage of anterograde and retrograde comets.
Draw lines from the proximal part of the process towards the distal part with respect to the nucleus for determining comet direction.
Display anterograde comets as directed from left to right on the kymograph.
Display retrograde comets as directed from right to left on the kymograph.
Report frame interval, number of analyzed frames, and duration of the analyzed substack in an Excel file.
Calculate process length by measuring the length of the drawn line for comet analysis.
Measure process width by determining the width of the drawn line for comet analysis.
Outline complete comets with the “Freehand line” tool on the Projected kymograph.
Add outlined comets to the ROI Manager from the "Tools" section in the "Analyze" menu.
Measure the length of growth (covered distance on the X axis) for each comet outlined in the Projected kymograph.
Measure the comet lifetime (projection on the Y axis of the comet trajectory).

Convert the value of the Comet lifetime from microns to seconds using the formula: [(Comet lifetime in microns × Duration of analyzed substack in seconds) / Value of the Y axis of the kymograph in microns].
Calculate the comet growth rate as Length of growth divided by Comet lifetime.
Calculate other desired parameters accordingly.
Open images of EB1 and Tyr-tubulin from immunostained microglia cells in ImageJ.
Invert LUT for the EB1 channel.
Identify EB1 comets at the plus end of tyrosinated microtubules using the signal of Tyr-tubulin as a reference.
Measure fluorescence intensity signal of EB1 at the tip of the microtubule defined by Tyr-tubulin.
Draw a line starting from the end of the comet proximal to the nucleus using the “Freehand line” tool.
Adjust the line width to cover the width of the comet.
Select clearly detectable comets, aiming for at least 100 comets from at least three independent experiments.
Use the “Plot profile” command from the “Analyze” menu to obtain a line scan for each comet.
Define the comet as Anterograde if the peak of the line scan is in the second half of the plot.
Define the comet as Retrograde if the peak of the line scan is not in the second half of the plot.
